Crie uma pagina para o PRO-SPEC framwork e inclua todo esse conteudo: The PRO-SPEC Framework Documentation that Codes Itself 1. Definition The PRO-SPEC is a single, standardized artifact (Markdown or YAML) that acts as both the Technical Documentation for humans and the Strict Context for AI. It solves the "Context Drift" problem in AI coding. Instead of chatting with an AI and losing details, you maintain a PRO-SPEC file. When you want code, you feed this file to the AI. It forces the AI to adhere to architectural, security, and performance standards defined in the spec, rather than guessing the implementation. The Golden Rule: The Code is merely a compilation of the PRO-SPEC. 2. The 5-Layer Architecture A PRO-SPEC is built on five layers. Layers 1-2 come from the X-SPEC (Documentation), and Layers 3-4 come from PROP (Engineering Constraints). Layer 1: The Intent (The Product Vibe) Purpose: Describes what and why. Components: User Stories, Business Logic, Success Metrics. Human Role: Written by PMs or Founders. Layer 2: The Contract (The Hard Spec) Purpose: Defines the rigid boundaries of the system. Components: Database Schemas, API Payloads (Input/Output), Route Definitions, TypeScript Interfaces. Human Role: Written by Lead Developers/Architects. Layer 3: The Shield (The Security PROP) Purpose: Defensive engineering constraints. Components: Auth logic, Data sanitization rules, Access control (RBAC), Secrets management. AI Instruction: "Reject any code generation that violates these constraints." Layer 4: The Engine (The Perf & UX PROP) Purpose: Optimization and usability standards. Components: Caching strategies, Complexity limits (Big O), Loading states, Error recovery flows, Accessibility (A11y). Layer 5: The Orchestration (The Command) Purpose: The trigger that tells the AI which role to adopt and what files to output. 3. The PRO-SPEC Template (Example) This is an example of a file named feature-chat.prospec.md that you would keep in your repository. codeMarkdown # PRO-SPEC: Real-Time Chat Module > Version: 1.2 | Stack: Node.js (NestJS) / React / PostgreSQL / Redis --- ## [L1] PRODUCT INTENT **User Story:** As a support agent, I want to receive messages in real-time without refreshing the page. **Business Logic:** - Messages must persist in the DB. - Unread counters must update instantly. - Support Agents have priority in the queue. --- ## [L2] TECHNICAL CONTRACTS **Database Model (Prisma Syntax):** ```prisma model Message { id String @id @default(uuid()) content String @db.VarChar(500) senderId String roomId String createdAt DateTime @default(now()) isRead Boolean @default(false) } API Interface (WS Event): Event: client:send_message Payload: { roomId: string, content: string } Response: server:message_ack or server:error [L3] THE SHIELD (Security Constraints) Instruction to AI: Apply these rules strictly. Fail generation if violated. Socket Auth: Handshake must validate JWT token from Authorization header. Disconnect immediately if invalid. Sanitization: All content strings must be stripped of HTML tags using sanitize-html library before DB insertion to prevent Stored XSS. Rate Limit: Max 10 messages per second per socket ID. Implement using Redis Leaky Bucket. Authorization: Verify senderId matches the JWT sub. User cannot send messages as someone else. [L4] THE ENGINE (Performance & UX Constraints) Optimistic UI: Frontend must append the message to the list immediately upon sending, then update status to "Delivered" on ACK. Virtualization: The message list component must use react-window to handle lists > 1000 items without DOM lag. Indexing: Ensure roomId and createdAt are composite indexed in Postgres for fast history retrieval. Edge Case: If WebSocket disconnects, queue outgoing messages in localStorage and retry automatically on reconnection. [L5] ORCHESTRATION Role: Senior FullStack Engineer. Task: Generate the following three files based strictly on this spec: chat.gateway.ts (Backend Logic) chat.service.ts (DB & Validation Logic) ChatWindow.tsx (Frontend Logic) Format: Return code blocks only. Add comments explaining where L3 and L4 constraints were applied. codeCode --- ## 4. The Workflow: From Vibe to Repo 1. **Drafting:** You (or an AI architect) write the `PRO-SPEC` file. 2. **Review:** A human reviews the Spec (Layers 2 & 3) to ensure the schema and security rules are correct. *This replaces code review.* 3. **Generation:** You paste the `PRO-SPEC` into your IDE's AI assistant (Cursor, Copilot) or a powerful LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o). 4. **Validation:** The code is generated. Because the strict constraints (Layers 3 & 4) were explicitly defined, the code is robust, secure, and matches the contract. 5. **Commit:** Both the `PRO-SPEC` file and the generated code are committed to the Git repository. The PRO-SPEC serves as the documentation for future developers. ## 5. Why PRO-SPEC is the Future * **It scales:** You can have a `PRO-SPEC` for the auth module, one for payments, one for the dashboard. * **It's agnostic:** You can switch AI models. The Spec remains the source of truth. * **It enforces seniority:** A Junior Dev using a Senior Architect's `PRO-SPEC` will generate Senior-level code. * **It's self-testing:** You can ask the AI: *"Write a Jest test suite that verifies 'L3-Rule-2' (Sanitization) from the PRO-SPEC."* The **PRO-SPEC** transforms the "Product Prompt" from a fleeting chat message into a tangible, version-controlled engineering asset.
